summary: Cited the extended boundary harness (receipt f394d8354fab48138079db19ca3deb13) in the replay-completion account, so its central quantitative claim now rests on two batch sizes. That receipt places the replay on both sides of the FSM channel's capacity at the library default of 64 batches: 8193 staged entries held 8192 tuples in 128 delivered batches and returned in 2ms (events 36-38), while 8194 staged entries held 8193 tuples in 129 delivered batches and did not return, with four stack samples naming the replay frames (events 39-41); the 16-batch pair reproduced in the same execution (holds at 32, violated at 35). The rationale now states the boundary as 128 delivered batches, that is 128 x MaxAppendEntries tuples - 2048 at 16 and 8192 at 64 - rather than a property of one setting, a counterevidence item records that those tuple counts are harness-derived at both sizes with one run per side at the larger one, and the limitation is restated to say which results remain single-setting (the batch size is now varied in the boundary and availability cases). joint_history records that the receipt is a revision of the boundary experiment whose harness adds the default-batch pair to the same file and that the two runs agree on both sides.
